<h1 id="openmeter-api">OpenMeter API v1.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

OpenMeter is a cloud native usage metering service.
The OpenMeter API allows you to ingest events, query meter usage, and manage resources.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://127.0.0.1">https://127.0.0.1</a> - Local

License: <a href="http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.html">Apache 2.0</a>

# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer Consumer portal token.

<h1 id="openmeter-api-subscriptions">Subscriptions</h1>

With Subscriptions, you can easily start, cancel, and manage customer subscriptions. For example, provisioning them on a specific plan or assigning custom rate cards.

## Create subscription

<a id="opIdcreateSubscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subscriptions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "alignment": {
      "billablesMustAlign": true
    },
    "metadata": {
      "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
    },
    "plan": {
      "key": "string",
      "version": 0
    },
    "startingPhase": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "settlementMode": {},
    "costBasisMode": "dynamic",
    "timing": "immediate",
    "customerId": "01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH",
    "customerKey": "string",
    "billingAnchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/subscriptions`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alignment": {
    "billablesMustAlign": true
  },
  "metadata": {
    "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
  },
  "plan": {
    "key": "string",
    "version": 0
  },
  "startingPhase": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "settlementMode": {},
  "costBasisMode": "dynamic",
  "timing": "immediate",
  "customerId": "01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH",
  "customerKey": "string",
  "billingAnchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
}
```

<h3 id="create-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SubscriptionCreate](#schemasubscriptioncreate)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[PlanSubscriptionCreate](#schemaplansubscriptioncreate)|false|Create subscription based on plan.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CustomSubscriptionCreate](#schemacustomsubscriptioncreate)|false|Create a custom subscription.|

<h3 id="create-subscription-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.|[Subscription](#schemasubscription)|
|400|Bad Request|The server cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error (e.g., malformed request syntax, invalid request message framing, or deceptive request routing). Variants with ErrorExtensions specific to subscriptions.|[SubscriptionBadRequestErrorResponse](#schemasubscriptionbadrequesterrorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request has not been applied because it lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource.|[UnauthorizedProblemResponse](#schemaunauthorizedproblemresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|The server understood the request but refuses to authorize it.|[ForbiddenProblemResponse](#schemaforbiddenproblemresponse)|
|409|Conflict|The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource.<br>Variants with ErrorExtensions specific to subscriptions.|[SubscriptionConflictErrorResponse](#schemasubscriptionconflicterrorresponse)|
|412|Precondition Failed|One or more conditions given in the request header fields evaluated to false when tested on the server.|[PreconditionFailedProblemResponse](#schemapreconditionfailedproblemresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request.|[InternalServerErrorProblemResponse](#schemainternalservererrorproblemresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|The server is currently unable to handle the request due to a temporary overload or scheduled maintenance, which will likely be alleviated after some delay.|[ServiceUnavailableProblemResponse](#schemaserviceunavailableproblemresponse)|
|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[UnexpectedProblemResponse](#schemaunexpectedproblemresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get subscription

<a id="opIdgetSubscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subscriptions/01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`

<h3 id="get-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscriptionId|path|string|true|none|
|at|query|string(date-time)|false|The time at which the subscription should be queried. If not provided the current time is used.|

`PATCH /api/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`

Batch processing commands for manipulating running subscriptions.
The key format is `/phases/{phaseKey}` or `/phases/{phaseKey}/items/{itemKey}`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "customizations": [
    {
      "op": "add_item",
      "phaseKey": "string",
      "rateCard": {
        "type": "flat_fee",
        "key": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "metadata": {
          "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
        },
        "featureKey": "string",
        "entitlementTemplate": {
          "metadata": {
            "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
          },
          "type": "metered",
          "isSoftLimit": false,
          "issueAfterReset": 0,
          "issueAfterResetPriority": 1,
          "preserveOverageAtReset": false,
          "usagePeriod": "string"
        },
        "taxConfig": {
          "behavior": {},
          "stripe": {
            "code": "txcd_10000000"
          },
          "customInvoicing": {
            "code": "string"
          },
          "taxCodeId": "01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH"
        },
        "billingCadence": "string",
        "price": {
          "type": "flat",
          "amount": "100",
          "paymentTerm": "in_arrears"
        },
        "discounts": {
          "percentage": {
            "percentage": {}
          },
          "usage": {
            "quantity": {}
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "timing": {}
}
```

<h3 id="edit-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscriptionId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[SubscriptionEdit](#schemasubscriptionedit)|true|none|
|» customizations|body|[[SubscriptionEditOperation](#schemasubscriptioneditoperation)]|true|Batch processing commands for manipulating running subscriptions.<br>The key format is `/phases/{phaseKey}` or `/phases/{phaseKey}/items/{itemKey}`.|
|» timing|body|object|false|Whether the billing period should be restarted.Timing configuration to allow for the changes to take effect at different times.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[SubscriptionTimingEnum](#schemasubscriptiontimingenum)|false|Subscription edit timing.<br>When immediate, the requested changes take effect immediately.<br>When nextBillingCycle, the requested changes take effect at the next billing cycle.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|[RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) formatted date-time string in UTC.|

|---|---|

`GET /api/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/addons`

|subscriptionId|path|string|true|none|

## Create subscription addon

<a id="opIdcreateSubscriptionAddon"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subscriptions/01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH/addons \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
    },
    "quantity": 1,
    "timing": {},
    "addon": {
      "id": "01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/addons`

Create a new subscription addon, either providing the key or the id of the addon.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
  },
  "quantity": 1,
  "timing": {},
  "addon": {
    "id": "01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-subscription-addon-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscriptionId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[SubscriptionAddonCreate](#schemasubscriptionaddoncreate)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable name for the resource. Between 1 and 256 characters.|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional description of the resource. Maximum 1024 characters.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Additional metadata for the resource.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» quantity|body|integer|true|The quantity of the add-on. Always 1 for single instance add-ons.|
|» timing|body|object|true|The timing of the operation. After the create or update, a new entry will be created in the timeline.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[SubscriptionTimingEnum](#schemasubscriptiontimingenum)|false|Subscription edit timing.<br>When immediate, the requested changes take effect immediately.<br>When nextBillingCycle, the requested changes take effect at the next billing cycle.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|[RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) formatted date-time string in UTC.|
|» addon|body|object|true|The add-on to create.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the add-on.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|immediate|
|» » *oneOf*|next_billing_cycle|

## Update subscription addon

<a id="opIdupdateSubscriptionAddon"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subscriptions/01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH/addons/01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
    },
    "quantity": 1,
    "timing": {}
  }'
```

`PATCH /api/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/addons/{subscriptionAddonId}`

Updates a subscription addon (allows changing the quantity: purchasing more instances or cancelling the current instances)

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
  },
  "quantity": 1,
  "timing": {}
}
```

<h3 id="update-subscription-addon-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscriptionId|path|string|true|none|
|subscriptionAddonId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[SubscriptionAddonUpdate](#schemasubscriptionaddonupdate)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Human-readable name for the resource. Between 1 and 256 characters.|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional description of the resource. Maximum 1024 characters.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Additional metadata for the resource.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» quantity|body|integer|false|The quantity of the add-on. Always 1 for single instance add-ons.|
|» timing|body|object|false|The timing of the operation. After the create or update, a new entry will be created in the timeline.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[SubscriptionTimingEnum](#schemasubscriptiontimingenum)|false|Subscription edit timing.<br>When immediate, the requested changes take effect immediately.<br>When nextBillingCycle, the requested changes take effect at the next billing cycle.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|[RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) formatted date-time string in UTC.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|immediate|
|» » *oneOf*|next_billing_cycle|

## Cancel subscription

<a id="opIdcancelSubscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subscriptions/01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "timing": {}
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/cancel`

Cancels the subscription.
Will result in a scheduling conflict if there are other subscriptions scheduled to start after the cancellation time.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "timing": {}
}
```

<h3 id="cancel-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscriptionId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» timing|body|object|false|If not provided the subscription is canceled immediately.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[SubscriptionTimingEnum](#schemasubscriptiontimingenum)|false|Subscription edit timing.<br>When immediate, the requested changes take effect immediately.<br>When nextBillingCycle, the requested changes take effect at the next billing cycle.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|[RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) formatted date-time string in UTC.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|immediate|
|» » *oneOf*|next_billing_cycle|

```bash
  -d '{

    },
    "metadata": {
      "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"

    "costBasisMode": "dynamic"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/change`

Closes a running subscription and starts a new one according to the specification.
Can be used for upgrades, downgrades, and plan changes.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "timing": {},
  "alignment": {
    "billablesMustAlign": true
  },
  "metadata": {
    "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
  },
  "plan": {
    "key": "string",
    "version": 0
  },
  "startingPhase": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "billingAnchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
  "settlementMode": {},
  "costBasisMode": "dynamic"
}
```

<h3 id="change-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscriptionId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[SubscriptionChange](#schemasubscriptionchange)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[PlanSubscriptionChange](#schemaplansubscriptionchange)|false|Change subscription based on plan.|
|» *oneOf*|body|[CustomSubscriptionChange](#schemacustomsubscriptionchange)|false|Change a custom subscription.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The request has succeeded.|[SubscriptionChangeResponseBody](#schemasubscriptionchangeresponsebody)|
|400|Bad Request|The server cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error (e.g., malformed request syntax, invalid request message framing, or deceptive request routing). Variants with ErrorExtensions specific to subscriptions.|[SubscriptionBadRequestErrorResponse](#schemasubscriptionbadrequesterrorresponse)|
|401|Unauthorized|The request has not been applied because it lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource.|[UnauthorizedProblemResponse](#schemaunauthorizedproblemresponse)|
|403|Forbidden|The server understood the request but refuses to authorize it.|[ForbiddenProblemResponse](#schemaforbiddenproblemresponse)|
|404|Not Found|The origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource or is not willing to disclose that one exists.|[NotFoundProblemResponse](#schemanotfoundproblemresponse)|
|409|Conflict|The request could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource.<br>Variants with ErrorExtensions specific to subscriptions.|[SubscriptionConflictErrorResponse](#schemasubscriptionconflicterrorresponse)|
|412|Precondition Failed|One or more conditions given in the request header fields evaluated to false when tested on the server.|[PreconditionFailedProblemResponse](#schemapreconditionfailedproblemresponse)|
|500|Internal Server Error|The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request.|[InternalServerErrorProblemResponse](#schemainternalservererrorproblemresponse)|
|503|Service Unavailable|The server is currently unable to handle the request due to a temporary overload or scheduled maintenance, which will likely be alleviated after some delay.|[ServiceUnavailableProblemResponse](#schemaserviceunavailableproblemresponse)|
|default|Default|An unexpected error response.|[UnexpectedProblemResponse](#schemaunexpectedproblemresponse)|

## Migrate subscription

<a id="opIdmigrateSubscription"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subscriptions/01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH/migrate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "timing": "immediate",
    "targetVersion": 1,
    "startingPhase": "string",
    "billingAnchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
```

`POST /api/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/migrate`

Migrates a running subscription to a later version of its current plan.
If startingPhase is omitted and billingAnchor is omitted or unchanged, the subscription is amended in place.
Unchanged items retain their service periods. Changed or removed items end at
the effective time; replacements and additions start from that time.
For in-place migrations, existing addons must be compatible with the target plan version.
The phase timeline, billing anchor, and subscription-level billing settings
are preserved. Both response entries refer to the same subscription:
current is the before snapshot and next is the amended view.
Providing startingPhase or a different billingAnchor uses subscription change: the current subscription
ends and a replacement starts at the effective time. This resets the phase timeline
and can produce billing adjustments. Addons are not transferred to the replacement.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "timing": "immediate",
  "targetVersion": 1,
  "startingPhase": "string",
  "billingAnchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
}
```

<h3 id="migrate-subscription-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subscriptionId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» timing|body|object|false|When the migration takes effect: immediately, at the next billing cycle, or at an explicit billing-aligned timestamp.<br>In-place migrations may be scheduled into a later phase when the current and target phase timelines match.<br>The target plan reference is saved immediately; changed items take effect at the requested time.<br>Past or unsupported times return an error.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[SubscriptionTimingEnum](#schemasubscriptiontimingenum)|false|Subscription edit timing.<br>When immediate, the requested changes take effect immediately.<br>When nextBillingCycle, the requested changes take effect at the next billing cycle.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|string(date-time)|false|[RFC3339](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3339) formatted date-time string in UTC.|
|» targetVersion|body|integer|false|A strictly later version of the current plan to migrate to.<br>If not provided, the subscription will migrate to the latest version of the current plan.|
|» startingPhase|body|string|false|Explicitly replace the subscription, starting in this target plan phase.<br>Providing this field always selects replacement, even if the phase matches the current one.<br>Replacement may produce billing adjustments and does not transfer addons.<br>Omit it to migrate in place; incompatible phase timelines then return an error.|
|» billingAnchor|body|string(date-time)|false|The anchor used with the plan's billing cadence to calculate billing periods.<br>If startingPhase is omitted and this anchor is omitted or equal to the existing one, migration preserves the current subscription.<br>Providing a different anchor ends the current subscription and creates a replacement.<br>The supplied anchor is preserved; it may be before or after the replacement's start time.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *oneOf*|immediate|
|» » *oneOf*|next_billing_cycle|

Variants with ErrorExtensions specific to subscriptions.|[SubscriptionBadRequestErrorResponse](#schemasubscriptionbadrequesterrorresponse)|

|403|Forbidden|The server understood the request but refuses to authorize it.|[ForbiddenProblemResponse](#schemaforbiddenproblemresponse)|

<h1 id="openmeter-api-subjects">Subjects</h1>

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Subjects as managable entities are being depracated, use customers with subject key usage attribution instead. 

 Subjects are entities that consume resources you wish to meter. These can range from users, servers, and services to devices. The design of subjects is intentionally generic, enabling flexible application across various metering scenarios. Typically, a subject acts as a unique identifier within your system for a user or customer. Meters are aggregating events for each subject.

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subjects \

  -d '[
    {
      "key": "customer-id",
      "displayName": "Customer Name",

      },
      "stripeCustomerId": "cus_JMOlctsKV8"
    }
  ]'
```

`POST /api/v1/subjects`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated

Upserts a subject. Creates or updates subject.

```json
  }
]
```

<h1 id="openmeter-api-product-catalog">Product Catalog</h1>

Configure and manage your product plans, pricing tiers, and subscription offerings. 

## List add-ons

<a id="opIdlistAddons"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/addons \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/addons`

List all add-ons.

<h3 id="list-add-ons-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|includeDeleted|query|boolean|false|Include deleted add-ons in response.<br><br>Usage: `?includeDeleted=true`|
|id|query|[string]|false|Filter by addon.id attribute|
|key|query|[string]|false|Filter by addon.key attribute|
|keyVersion|query|object|false|Filter by addon.key and addon.version attributes|
|status|query|[[AddonStatus](#schemaaddonstatus)]|false|Only return add-ons with the given status.<br><br>Usage:<br>- `?status=active`: return only the currently active add-ons<br>- `?status=draft`: return only the draft add-ons<br>- `?status=archived`: return only the archived add-ons|
|currency|query|[[CurrencyCode](#schemacurrencycode)]|false|Filter by addon.currency attribute|
|page|query|integer|false|Page index.<br><br>Default is 1.|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items per page.<br><br>Default is 100.|
|order|query|object|false|The order direction.|
|orderBy|query|[AddonOrderBy](#schemaaddonorderby)|false|The order by field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|draft|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|orderBy|id|
|orderBy|key|
|orderBy|version|
|orderBy|created_at|
|orderBy|updated_at|

## Create feature

<a id="opIdcreateFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/features \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "key": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "metadata": {
      "key": "value"
    },
    "meterSlug": "tokens_total",
    "meterGroupByFilters": {
      "model": "gpt-4",
      "type": "input"
    },
    "advancedMeterGroupByFilters": {
      "model": {
        "$in": [
          "gpt-4",
          "gpt-4o"
        ]
      },
      "type": {
        "$eq": "input"
      }
    },
    "unitCost": {
      "type": "manual",
      "amount": {}
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/features`

Features are either metered or static. A feature is metered if meterSlug is provided at creation.
For metered features you can pass additional filters that will be applied when calculating feature usage, based on the meter's groupBy fields.
Meters with SUM, COUNT, UNIQUE_COUNT and LATEST aggregations are supported for features.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "key": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "key": "value"
  },
  "meterSlug": "tokens_total",
  "meterGroupByFilters": {
    "model": "gpt-4",
    "type": "input"
  },
  "advancedMeterGroupByFilters": {
    "model": {
      "$in": [
        "gpt-4",
        "gpt-4o"
      ]
    },
    "type": {
      "$eq": "input"
    }
  },
  "unitCost": {
    "type": "manual",
    "amount": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[FeatureCreateInputs](#schemafeaturecreateinputs)|true|none|
|» key|body|string|true|A key is a unique string that is used to identify a resource.|
|» name|body|string|true|none|
|» metadata|body|object|false|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» meterSlug|body|string|false|A key is a unique string that is used to identify a resource.|
|» meterGroupByFilters|body|object|false|**Deprecated.** Optional meter group by filters.<br>Useful if the meter scope is broader than what feature tracks.<br>Example scenario would be a meter tracking all token use with groupBy fields for the model,<br>then the feature could filter for model=gpt-4.<br><br>⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use advancedMeterGroupByFilters instead|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» advancedMeterGroupByFilters|body|object|false|Optional advanced meter group by filters.<br>You can use this to filter for values of the meter groupBy fields.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[FilterString](#schemafilterstring)|false|A filter for a string field.|
|» unitCost|body|object|false|Optional per-unit cost configuration.<br>Use "manual" for a fixed per-unit cost, or "llm" to look up cost<br>from the LLM cost database based on meter group-by properties.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[FeatureManualUnitCost](#schemafeaturemanualunitcost)|false|A fixed per-unit cost amount.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[FeatureLLMUnitCost](#schemafeaturellmunitcost)|false|LLM cost lookup configuration.<br>Maps meter group-by dimensions to LLM cost database fields.|

## Delete feature

<a id="opIddeleteFeature"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/features/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/problem+json'
```

`DELETE /api/v1/features/{featureId}`

Archive a feature by ID.

Once a feature is archived it cannot be unarchived. If a feature is archived, new entitlements cannot be created for it, but archiving the feature does not affect existing entitlements.
This means, if you want to create a new feature with the same key, and then create entitlements for it, the previous entitlements have to be deleted first on a per subject basis.

<h3 id="delete-feature-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|featureId|path|string|true|none|

## List plans

<a id="opIdlistPlans"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/plans \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/plans`

List all plans.

<h3 id="list-plans-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|includeDeleted|query|boolean|false|Include deleted plans in response.<br><br>Usage: `?includeDeleted=true`|
|id|query|[string]|false|Filter by plan.id attribute|
|key|query|[string]|false|Filter by plan.key attribute|
|keyVersion|query|object|false|Filter by plan.key and plan.version attributes|
|status|query|[[PlanStatus](#schemaplanstatus)]|false|Only return plans with the given status.<br><br>Usage:<br>- `?status=active`: return only the currently active plan<br>- `?status=draft`: return only the draft plan<br>- `?status=archived`: return only the archived plans|
|currency|query|[[CurrencyCode](#schemacurrencycode)]|false|Filter by plan.currency attribute|
|page|query|integer|false|Page index.<br><br>Default is 1.|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items per page.<br><br>Default is 100.|
|order|query|object|false|The order direction.|
|orderBy|query|[PlanOrderBy](#schemaplanorderby)|false|The order by field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|draft|
|status|active|
|status|archived|
|status|scheduled|
|orderBy|id|

|orderBy|created_at|

|» key|body|string|true|A semi-unique identifier for the resource.|
|» alignment|body|object|false|Alignment configuration for the plan.|
|» » billablesMustAlign|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Whether all Billable items and RateCards must align.<br>Alignment means the Price's BillingCadence must align for both duration and anchor time.|
|» currency|body|object|true|The currency code of the plan.|
|» billingCadence|body|string(duration)|true|The default billing cadence for subscriptions using this plan.<br>Defines how often customers are billed using ISO8601 duration format.<br>Examples: "P1M" (monthly), "P3M" (quarterly), "P1Y" (annually).|
|» proRatingConfig|body|object|false|Default pro-rating configuration for subscriptions using this plan.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether pro-rating is enabled for this plan.|
|» » mode|body|object|true|How to handle pro-rating for billing period changes.|
|» settlementMode|body|object|false|The settlement mode of the plan.<br>It determines how the billing system generates invoices and credits for the subscriptions using this plan.<br>- credit_then_invoice: credits from the previous billing period are applied first, then the remaining balance is invoiced.<br>- credit_only: only credits from the previous billing period are generated and applied. No invoices are generated for the subscription.<br>This is the default and most common settlement mode.|
|» phases|body|[[PlanPhase](#schemaplanphase)]|true|The plan phase or pricing ramp allows changing a plan's rate cards over time as a subscription progresses.<br>A phase switch occurs only at the end of a billing period, ensuring that a single subscription invoice will not include charges from different phase prices.|

<h3 id="update-a-plan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|planId|path|string|true|none|

|» name|body|string|true|Human-readable name for the resource. Between 1 and 256 characters.|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional description of the resource. Maximum 1024 characters.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Additional metadata for the resource.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» alignment|body|object|false|Alignment configuration for the plan.|
|» » billablesMustAlign|body|boolean|false|**Deprecated.** Whether all Billable items and RateCards must align.<br>Alignment means the Price's BillingCadence must align for both duration and anchor time.|
|» billingCadence|body|string(duration)|true|The default billing cadence for subscriptions using this plan.<br>Defines how often customers are billed using ISO8601 duration format.<br>Examples: "P1M" (monthly), "P3M" (quarterly), "P1Y" (annually).|
|» proRatingConfig|body|object|false|Default pro-rating configuration for subscriptions using this plan.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether pro-rating is enabled for this plan.|
|» » mode|body|object|true|How to handle pro-rating for billing period changes.|
|» settlementMode|body|object|false|The settlement mode of the plan.<br>It determines how the billing system generates invoices and credits for the subscriptions using this plan.<br>- credit_then_invoice: credits from the previous billing period are applied first, then the remaining balance is invoiced.<br>- credit_only: only credits from the previous billing period are generated and applied. No invoices are generated for the subscription.<br>This is the default and most common settlement mode.|
|» phases|body|[[PlanPhase](#schemaplanphase)]|true|The plan phase or pricing ramp allows changing a plan's rate cards over time as a subscription progresses.<br>A phase switch occurs only at the end of a billing period, ensuring that a single subscription invoice will not include charges from different phase prices.|

<h1 id="openmeter-api-portal">Portal</h1>

With the Consumer Portal, you can build in-app user-facing dashboards where your users can track their usage in real-time. Subject scoped portal tokens can be generated on your behalf to allow restricted access to the OpenMeter API.

## Query meter Query meter

<a id="opIdqueryPortalMeter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/portal/meters/string/query \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /api/v1/portal/meters/{meterSlug}/query`

Query meter for consumer portal. This endpoint is publicly exposable to consumers. Query meter for consumer portal. This endpoint is publicly exposable to consumers.

<h3 id="query-meter-query-meter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|meterSlug|path|string|true|none|
|clientId|query|string|false|Client ID<br>Useful to track progress of a query.|
|from|query|string(date-time)|false|Start date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.<br><br>For example: ?from=2025-01-01T00%3A00%3A00.000Z|
|to|query|string(date-time)|false|End date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.<br><br>For example: ?to=2025-02-01T00%3A00%3A00.000Z|
|windowSize|query|[WindowSize](#schemawindowsize)|false|If not specified, a single usage aggregate will be returned for the entirety of the specified period for each subject and group.<br><br>For example: ?windowSize=DAY|
|windowTimeZone|query|string|false|The value is the name of the time zone as defined in the IANA Time Zone Database (http://www.iana.org/time-zones).<br>If not specified, the UTC timezone will be used.<br><br>For example: ?windowTimeZone=UTC|
|filterCustomerId|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple customers.<br><br>For example: ?filterCustomerId=customer-1&filterCustomerId=customer-2|
|filterGroupBy|query|object|false|**Deprecated.** Simple filter for group bys with exact match.<br><br>For example: ?filterGroupBy[vendor]=openai&filterGroupBy[model]=gpt-4-turbo<br><br>⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use `advancedMeterGroupByFilters` instead|
|advancedMeterGroupByFilters|query|object(application/json)|false|Optional advanced meter group by filters.<br>You can use this to filter for values of the meter groupBy fields.|
|groupBy|query|[string]|false|If not specified a single aggregate will be returned for each subject and time window.<br>`subject` is a reserved group by value.<br><br>For example: ?groupBy=subject&groupBy=model|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|windowSize|MINUTE|
|windowSize|HOUR|
|windowSize|DAY|
|windowSize|MONTH|

```json
      "value": 12,
      "windowStart": "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "windowEnd": "2023-01-02T00:00:00Z",
```

<h1 id="openmeter-api-notifications">Notifications</h1>

Notifications provide automated triggers when specific entitlement balances and usage thresholds are reached, ensuring that your customers and sales teams are always informed. Notify customers and internal teams when specific conditions are met, like reaching 75%, 100%, and 150% of their monthly usage allowance. [Read more](https://openmeter.io/docs/guides/notifications/overview).

## List notification channels

<a id="opIdlistNotificationChannels"></a>

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

## List notification events

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/notification/events \
```

`GET /api/v1/notification/events`

List all notification events.

<h3 id="list-notification-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|from|query|string(date-time)|false|Start date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br>Inclusive.|
|to|query|string(date-time)|false|End date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br>Inclusive.|
|feature|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple feature ids or keys.<br><br>Usage: `?feature=feature-1&feature=feature-2`|
|subject|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple subject ids or keys.<br><br>Usage: `?subject=subject-1&subject=subject-2`|
|rule|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple rule ids.<br><br>Usage: `?rule=01J8J2XYZ2N5WBYK09EDZFBSZM&rule=01J8J4R4VZH180KRKQ63NB2VA5`|
|channel|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple channel ids.<br><br>Usage: `?channel=01J8J4RXH778XB056JS088PCYT&channel=01J8J4S1R1G9EVN62RG23A9M6J`|
|page|query|integer|false|Page index.<br><br>Default is 1.|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items per page.<br><br>Default is 100.|
|order|query|object|false|The order direction.|
|orderBy|query|[NotificationEventOrderBy](#schemanotificationeventorderby)|false|The order by field.|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

<h1 id="openmeter-api-meters">Meters</h1>

Meters specify how to aggregate events for billing and analytics purposes. Meters can be configured with multiple aggregation methods and groupings. Multiple meters can be created for the same event type, enabling flexible metering scenarios.

## List meters

<a id="opIdlistMeters"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/meters \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/meters`

List meters.

<h3 id="list-meters-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|Page index.<br><br>Default is 1.|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items per page.<br><br>Default is 100.|
|order|query|object|false|The order direction.|
|orderBy|query|[MeterOrderBy](#schemameterorderby)|false|The order by field.|
|includeDeleted|query|boolean|false|Include deleted meters.|

#### Enumerated Values

|orderBy|key|
|orderBy|name|
|orderBy|aggregation|
|orderBy|createdAt|
|orderBy|updatedAt|

## Create meter

<a id="opIdcreateMeter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/meters \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "slug": "tokens_total",
    "name": "Tokens Total",
    "description": "AI Token Usage",
    "aggregation": "SUM",
    "eventType": "prompt",
    "valueProperty": "$.tokens",
    "groupBy": {
      "model": "$.model",
      "type": "$.type"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/meters`

Create a meter.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "slug": "tokens_total",
  "name": "Tokens Total",
  "description": "AI Token Usage",
  "aggregation": "SUM",
  "eventType": "prompt",
  "valueProperty": "$.tokens",
  "groupBy": {
    "model": "$.model",
    "type": "$.type"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-meter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[MeterCreate](#schemametercreate)|true|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Optional description of the resource. Maximum 1024 characters.|
|» metadata|body|object \| null|false|Additional metadata for the resource.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|Human-readable name for the resource. Between 1 and 256 characters.<br>Defaults to the slug if not specified.|
|» slug|body|string|true|A unique, human-readable identifier for the meter.<br>Must consist only alphanumeric and underscore characters.|
|» aggregation|body|object|true|The aggregation type to use for the meter.|
|» eventType|body|string|true|The event type to aggregate.|
|» eventFrom|body|string(date-time)|false|The date since the meter should include events.<br>Useful to skip old events.<br>If not specified, all historical events are included.|
|» valueProperty|body|string|false|JSONPath expression to extract the value from the ingested event's data property.<br><br>The ingested value for SUM, AVG, MIN, and MAX aggregations is a number or a string that can be parsed to a number.<br><br>For UNIQUE_COUNT aggregation, the ingested value must be a string. For COUNT aggregation the valueProperty is ignored.|
|» groupBy|body|object|false|Named JSONPath expressions to extract the group by values from the event data.<br><br>Keys must be unique and consist only alphanumeric and underscore characters.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|

## Query meter

<a id="opIdqueryMeter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/meters/string/query \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/meters/{meterIdOrSlug}/query`

Query meter for usage.

<h3 id="query-meter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|meterIdOrSlug|path|string|true|none|
|clientId|query|string|false|Client ID<br>Useful to track progress of a query.|
|from|query|string(date-time)|false|Start date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.<br><br>For example: ?from=2025-01-01T00%3A00%3A00.000Z|
|to|query|string(date-time)|false|End date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.<br><br>For example: ?to=2025-02-01T00%3A00%3A00.000Z|
|windowSize|query|[WindowSize](#schemawindowsize)|false|If not specified, a single usage aggregate will be returned for the entirety of the specified period for each subject and group.<br><br>For example: ?windowSize=DAY|
|windowTimeZone|query|string|false|The value is the name of the time zone as defined in the IANA Time Zone Database (http://www.iana.org/time-zones).<br>If not specified, the UTC timezone will be used.<br><br>For example: ?windowTimeZone=UTC|
|subject|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple subjects.<br><br>For example: ?subject=subject-1&subject=subject-2|
|filterCustomerId|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple customers.<br><br>For example: ?filterCustomerId=customer-1&filterCustomerId=customer-2|
|filterGroupBy|query|object|false|**Deprecated.** Simple filter for group bys with exact match.<br><br>For example: ?filterGroupBy[vendor]=openai&filterGroupBy[model]=gpt-4-turbo<br><br>⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use `advancedMeterGroupByFilters` instead|
|advancedMeterGroupByFilters|query|object(application/json)|false|Optional advanced meter group by filters.<br>You can use this to filter for values of the meter groupBy fields.|
|groupBy|query|[string]|false|If not specified a single aggregate will be returned for each subject and time window.<br>`subject` is a reserved group by value.<br><br>For example: ?groupBy=subject&groupBy=model|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|windowSize|MINUTE|
|windowSize|HOUR|
|windowSize|DAY|
|windowSize|MONTH|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "from": "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "to": "2023-01-02T00:00:00Z",
  "windowSize": "DAY",
  "data": [
    {
      "value": 12,
      "windowStart": "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "windowEnd": "2023-01-02T00:00:00Z",
      "subject": "customer-1",
      "groupBy": {
        "model": "gpt-4-turbo",
        "type": "prompt"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
  "type": "about:blank",

  "instance": "urn:request:local/JMOlctsKV8-000001",
  "extensions": {
    "validationErrors": [
```

## Query meter

<a id="opIdqueryMeterPost"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/meters/string/query \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "clientId": "f74e58ed-94ce-4041-ae06-cf45420451a3",
    "from": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
    "to": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
    "windowSize": "DAY",
    "windowTimeZone": "UTC",
    "subject": [
      "subject-1",
      "subject-2"
    ],
    "filterCustomerId": [
      "id-1",
      "id-2"
    ],
    "filterGroupBy": {
      "model": [
        "gpt-4-turbo",
        "gpt-4o"
      ],
      "type": [
        "prompt"
      ]
    },
    "advancedMeterGroupByFilters": {
      "model": {
        "$in": [
          "gpt-4",
          "gpt-4o"
        ]
      },
      "type": {
        "$eq": "input"
      }
    },
    "groupBy": [
      "model",
      "type"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/meters/{meterIdOrSlug}/query`

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "clientId": "f74e58ed-94ce-4041-ae06-cf45420451a3",
  "from": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
  "to": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
  "windowSize": "DAY",
  "windowTimeZone": "UTC",
  "subject": [
    "subject-1",
    "subject-2"
  ],
  "filterCustomerId": [
    "id-1",
    "id-2"
  ],
  "filterGroupBy": {
    "model": [
      "gpt-4-turbo",
      "gpt-4o"
    ],
    "type": [
      "prompt"
    ]
  },
  "advancedMeterGroupByFilters": {
    "model": {
      "$in": [
        "gpt-4",
        "gpt-4o"
      ]
    },
    "type": {
      "$eq": "input"
    }
  },
  "groupBy": [
    "model",
    "type"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="query-meter-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|meterIdOrSlug|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[MeterQueryRequest](#schemameterqueryrequest)|true|none|
|» clientId|body|string|false|Client ID<br>Useful to track progress of a query.|
|» from|body|string(date-time)|false|Start date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.|
|» to|body|string(date-time)|false|End date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.|
|» windowSize|body|object|false|If not specified, a single usage aggregate will be returned for the entirety of the specified period for each subject and group.|
|» windowTimeZone|body|string|false|The value is the name of the time zone as defined in the IANA Time Zone Database (http://www.iana.org/time-zones).<br>If not specified, the UTC timezone will be used.|
|» subject|body|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple subjects.|
|» filterCustomerId|body|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple customers.|
|» filterGroupBy|body|object|false|Simple filter for group bys with exact match.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[string]|false|none|
|» advancedMeterGroupByFilters|body|object|false|Optional advanced meter group by filters.<br>You can use this to filter for values of the meter groupBy fields.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|[FilterString](#schemafilterstring)|false|A filter for a string field.|
|» groupBy|body|[string]|false|If not specified a single aggregate will be returned for each subject and time window.<br>`subject` is a reserved group by value.|

```json
    {
      "value": 12,
      "windowStart": "2023-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "windowEnd": "2023-01-02T00:00:00Z",
      "subject": "customer-1",
      "groupBy": {
        "model": "gpt-4-turbo",

}
```

<h1 id="openmeter-api-events">Events</h1>

Events are used to track usage of your product or service. Events are processed asynchronously by the meters, so they may not be immediately available for querying.

## List ingested events

<a id="opIdlistEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/events`

List ingested events within a time range.

If the from query param is not provided it defaults to last 72 hours.

<h3 id="list-ingested-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clientId|query|string|false|Client ID<br>Useful to track progress of a query.|
|ingestedAtFrom|query|string(date-time)|false|Start date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.|
|ingestedAtTo|query|string(date-time)|false|End date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.|
|id|query|string|false|The event ID.<br><br>Accepts partial ID.|
|subject|query|string|false|The event subject.<br><br>Accepts partial subject.|
|customerId|query|[string]|false|The event customer ID.|
|from|query|string(date-time)|false|Start date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.|
|to|query|string(date-time)|false|End date-time in RFC 3339 format.<br><br>Inclusive.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Number of events to return.|

```bash
  }'
```

## List all entitlements

<a id="opIdlistEntitlements"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/entitlements \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/entitlements`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

List all entitlements for all the subjects and features. This endpoint is intended for administrative purposes only.
To fetch the entitlements of a specific subject please use the /api/v1/subjects/{subjectKeyOrID}/entitlements endpoint.
If page is provided that takes precedence and the paginated response is returned.

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use [`GET /api/v2/entitlements`](#tag/entitlements/get/api/v2/entitlements) instead.

<h3 id="list-all-entitlements-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|feature|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple features.<br><br>Usage: `?feature=feature-1&feature=feature-2`|
|subject|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple subjects.<br><br>Usage: `?subject=customer-1&subject=customer-2`|
|entitlementType|query|[[EntitlementType](#schemaentitlementtype)]|false|Filtering by multiple entitlement types.<br><br>Usage: `?entitlementType=metered&entitlementType=boolean`|
|excludeInactive|query|boolean|false|Exclude inactive entitlements in the response (those scheduled for later or earlier)|
|page|query|integer|false|Page index.<br><br>Default is 1.|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items per page.<br><br>Default is 100.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Number of items to skip.<br><br>Default is 0.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Number of items to return.<br><br>Default is 100.|
|order|query|object|false|The order direction.|
|orderBy|query|[EntitlementOrderBy](#schemaentitlementorderby)|false|The order by field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|entitlementType|metered|
|entitlementType|boolean|
|entitlementType|static|
|orderBy|createdAt|
|orderBy|updatedAt|

## List grants

<a id="opIdlistGrants"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/grants \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/grants`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

List all grants for all the subjects and entitlements. This endpoint is intended for administrative purposes only.
To fetch the grants of a specific entitlement please use the /api/v1/subjects/{subjectKeyOrID}/entitlements/{entitlementOrFeatureID}/grants endpoint.
If page is provided that takes precedence and the paginated response is returned.

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use [`GET /api/v2/grants`](#tag/entitlements/get/api/v2/grants) instead.

<h3 id="list-grants-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|feature|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple features.<br><br>Usage: `?feature=feature-1&feature=feature-2`|
|subject|query|[string]|false|Filtering by multiple subjects.<br><br>Usage: `?subject=customer-1&subject=customer-2`|
|includeDeleted|query|boolean|false|Include deleted|
|page|query|integer|false|Page index.<br><br>Default is 1.|
|pageSize|query|integer|false|The maximum number of items per page.<br><br>Default is 100.|
|offset|query|integer|false|Number of items to skip.<br><br>Default is 0.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Number of items to return.<br><br>Default is 100.|
|order|query|object|false|The order direction.|
|orderBy|query|[GrantOrderBy](#schemagrantorderby)|false|The order by field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|orderBy|id|
|orderBy|createdAt|
|orderBy|updatedAt|

## Void grant

<a id="opIdvoidGrant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/grants/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/problem+json'
```

`DELETE /api/v1/grants/{grantId}`

Voiding a grant means it is no longer valid, it doesn't take part in further balance calculations. Voiding a grant does not retroactively take effect, meaning any usage that has already been attributed to the grant will remain, but future usage cannot be burnt down from the grant.
For example, if you have a single grant for your metered entitlement with an initial amount of 100, and so far 60 usage has been metered, the grant (and the entitlement itself) would have a balance of 40. If you then void that grant, balance becomes 0, but the 60 previous usage will not be affected.

<h3 id="void-grant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|grantId|path|string|true|none|
|at|query|string(date-time)|false|The time at which the grant should be voided.<br>Must not be in the future and must be within the current usage period of the entitlement.<br>Defaults to the current time if not specified.|

## Create a subject entitlement

<a id="opIdcreateEntitlement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subjects/string/entitlements \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "featureKey": "example-feature-key",
    "featureId": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
    "metadata": {
      "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
    },
    "type": "metered",
    "isSoftLimit": false,
    "isUnlimited": false,
    "usagePeriod": {
      "interval": "DAY",
      "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
    },
    "measureUsageFrom": {},
    "issueAfterReset": 0,
    "issueAfterResetPriority": 1,
    "preserveOverageAtReset": false
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/subjects/{subjectIdOrKey}/entitlements`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

OpenMeter has three types of entitlements: metered, boolean, and static. The type property determines the type of entitlement. The underlying feature has to be compatible with the entitlement type specified in the request (e.g., a metered entitlement needs a feature associated with a meter).

- Boolean entitlements define static feature access, e.g. "Can use SSO authentication".
- Static entitlements let you pass along a configuration while granting access, e.g. "Using this feature with X Y settings" (passed in the config).
- Metered entitlements have many use cases, from setting up usage-based access to implementing complex credit systems.  Example: The customer can use 10000 AI tokens during the usage period of the entitlement.

A given subject can only have one active (non-deleted) entitlement per featureKey. If you try to create a new entitlement for a featureKey that already has an active entitlement, the request will fail with a 409 error.

Once an entitlement is created you cannot modify it, only delete it.

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use [`POST /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements`](#tag/entitlements/post/api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements) instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "featureKey": "example-feature-key",
  "featureId": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "metadata": {
    "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
  },
  "type": "metered",
  "isSoftLimit": false,
  "isUnlimited": false,
  "usagePeriod": {
    "interval": "DAY",
    "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
  },
  "measureUsageFrom": {},
  "issueAfterReset": 0,
  "issueAfterResetPriority": 1,
  "preserveOverageAtReset": false
}
```

## Create subject entitlement grant

<a id="opIdcreateGrant"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subjects/string/entitlements/string/grants \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "amount": 100,
    "priority": 1,
    "effectiveAt": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
    "expiration": {
      "duration": {},
      "count": 12
    },
    "maxRolloverAmount": 100,
    "minRolloverAmount": 100,
    "metadata": {
      "stripePaymentId": "pi_4OrAkhLvyihio9p51h9iiFnB"
    },
    "recurrence": {
      "interval": "DAY",
      "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/subjects/{subjectIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/grants`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Grants define a behavior of granting usage for a metered entitlement. They can have complicated recurrence and rollover rules, thanks to which you can define a wide range of access patterns with a single grant, in most cases you don't have to periodically create new grants. You can only issue grants for active metered entitlements.

A grant defines a given amount of usage that can be consumed for the entitlement. The grant is in effect between its effective date and its expiration date. Specifying both is mandatory for new grants.

Grants have a priority setting that determines their order of use. Lower numbers have higher priority, with 0 being the highest priority.

Grants can have a recurrence setting intended to automate the manual reissuing of grants. For example, a daily recurrence is equal to reissuing that same grant every day (ignoring rollover settings).

Rollover settings define what happens to the remaining balance of a grant at a reset. Balance_After_Reset = MIN(MaxRolloverAmount, MAX(Balance_Before_Reset, MinRolloverAmount))

Grants cannot be changed once created, only deleted. This is to ensure that balance is deterministic regardless of when it is queried.

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use [`POST /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/grants`](#tag/entitlements/post/api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/grants) instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 100,
  "priority": 1,
  "effectiveAt": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
  "expiration": {
    "duration": {},
    "count": 12
  },
  "maxRolloverAmount": 100,
  "minRolloverAmount": 100,
  "metadata": {
    "stripePaymentId": "pi_4OrAkhLvyihio9p51h9iiFnB"
  },
  "recurrence": {
    "interval": "DAY",
    "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-subject-entitlement-grant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subjectIdOrKey|path|string|true|none|
|entitlementIdOrFeatureKey|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[EntitlementGrantCreateInput](#schemaentitlementgrantcreateinput)|true|none|
|» amount|body|number(double)|true|The amount to grant. Should be a positive number.|
|» priority|body|integer(uint8)|false|The priority of the grant. Grants with higher priority are applied first.<br>Priority is a positive decimal numbers. With lower numbers indicating higher importance.<br>For example, a priority of 1 is more urgent than a priority of 2.<br>When there are several grants available for the same subject, the system selects the grant with the highest priority.<br>In cases where grants share the same priority level, the grant closest to its expiration will be used first.<br>In the case of two grants have identical priorities and expiration dates, the system will use the grant that was created first.|
|» effectiveAt|body|string(date-time)|true|Effective date for grants and anchor for recurring grants. Provided value will be ceiled to metering windowSize (minute).|
|» expiration|body|object|true|The grant expiration definition|
|» » duration|body|object|true|The unit of time for the expiration period.|
|» » count|body|integer(uint32)|true|The number of time units in the expiration period.|
|» maxRolloverAmount|body|number(double)|false|Grants are rolled over at reset, after which they can have a different balance compared to what they had before the reset.<br>Balance after the reset is calculated as: Balance_After_Reset = MIN(MaxRolloverAmount, MAX(Balance_Before_Reset, MinRolloverAmount))|
|» minRolloverAmount|body|number(double)|false|Grants are rolled over at reset, after which they can have a different balance compared to what they had before the reset.<br>Balance after the reset is calculated as: Balance_After_Reset = MIN(MaxRolloverAmount, MAX(Balance_Before_Reset, MinRolloverAmount))|
|» metadata|body|object|false|The grant metadata.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» recurrence|body|object|false|The subject of the grant.|
|» » interval|body|object|true|The unit of time for the interval.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|[RecurringPeriodIntervalEnum](#schemarecurringperiodintervalenum)|false|The unit of time for the interval.<br>One of: `day`, `week`, `month`, or `year`.|
|» » anchor|body|string(date-time)|false|A date-time anchor to base the recurring period on.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » *anyOf*|DAY|
|» » » *anyOf*|WEEK|
|» » » *anyOf*|MONTH|
|» » » *anyOf*|YEAR|

## Override subject entitlement

<a id="opIdoverrideEntitlement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subjects/string/entitlements/string/override \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "featureKey": "example-feature-key",
    "featureId": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
    "metadata": {
      "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
    },
    "type": "metered",
    "isSoftLimit": false,
    "isUnlimited": false,
    "usagePeriod": {
      "interval": "DAY",
      "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
    },
    "measureUsageFrom": {},
    "issueAfterReset": 0,
    "issueAfterResetPriority": 1,
    "preserveOverageAtReset": false
  }'
```

`PUT /api/v1/subjects/{subjectIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/override`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Overriding an entitlement creates a new entitlement from the provided inputs and soft deletes the previous entitlement for the provided subject-feature pair. If the previous entitlement is already deleted or otherwise doesnt exist, the override will fail.

This endpoint is useful for upgrades, downgrades, or other changes to entitlements that require a new entitlement to be created with zero downtime.

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use [`PUT /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/override`](#tag/entitlements/put/api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/override) instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "featureKey": "example-feature-key",
  "featureId": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "metadata": {
    "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
  },
  "type": "metered",
  "isSoftLimit": false,
  "isUnlimited": false,
  "usagePeriod": {
    "interval": "DAY",
    "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
  },
  "measureUsageFrom": {},
  "issueAfterReset": 0,
  "issueAfterResetPriority": 1,
  "preserveOverageAtReset": false
}
```

<h3 id="override-subject-entitlement-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subjectIdOrKey|path|string|true|none|
|entitlementIdOrFeatureKey|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[EntitlementCreateInputs](#schemaentitlementcreateinputs)|true|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|[EntitlementMeteredCreateInputs](#schemaentitlementmeteredcreateinputs)|false|**Deprecated.** Create inpurs for metered entitlement|
|» *oneOf*|body|[EntitlementStaticCreateInputs](#schemaentitlementstaticcreateinputs)|false|**Deprecated.** Create inputs for static entitlement|
|» *oneOf*|body|[EntitlementBooleanCreateInputs](#schemaentitlementbooleancreateinputs)|false|**Deprecated.** Create inputs for boolean entitlement|

## Get subject entitlement value

<a id="opIdgetEntitlementValue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subjects/string/entitlements/string/value \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/subjects/{subjectIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/value`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

This endpoint should be used for access checks and enforcement. All entitlement types share the hasAccess property in their value response, but multiple other properties are returned based on the entitlement type.

For convenience reasons, /value works with both entitlementId and featureKey.

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use [`GET /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/value`](#tag/entitlements/get/api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/value) instead.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|subjectIdOrKey|path|string|true|none|
|entitlementIdOrFeatureKey|path|string|true|none|
|time|query|string(date-time)|false|none|

## Delete subject entitlement

<a id="opIddeleteEntitlement"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subjects/string/entitlements/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/problem+json'
```

`DELETE /api/v1/subjects/{subjectIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementId}`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Deleting an entitlement revokes access to the associated feature. As a single subject can only have one entitlement per featureKey, when "migrating" features you have to delete the old entitlements as well.
As access and status checks can be historical queries, deleting an entitlement populates the deletedAt timestamp. When queried for a time before that, the entitlement is still considered active, you cannot have retroactive changes to access, which is important for, among other things, auditing.

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use [`DELETE /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}`](#tag/entitlements/delete/api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}) instead.

<h3 id="delete-subject-entitlement-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subjectIdOrKey|path|string|true|none|
|entitlementId|path|string|true|none|

## Get subject entitlement history

<a id="opIdgetEntitlementHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subjects/string/entitlements/string/history?windowSize=MINUTE' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/subjects/{subjectIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementId}/history`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Returns historical balance and usage data for the entitlement. The queried history can span accross multiple reset events.

BurndownHistory returns a continous history of segments, where the segments are seperated by events that changed either the grant burndown priority or the usage period.

WindowedHistory returns windowed usage data for the period enriched with balance information and the list of grants that were being burnt down in that window.

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use [`GET /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/history`](#tag/entitlements/get/api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/history) instead.

<h3 id="get-subject-entitlement-history-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subjectIdOrKey|path|string|true|none|
|entitlementId|path|string|true|none|
|from|query|string(date-time)|false|Start of time range to query entitlement: date-time in RFC 3339 format. Defaults to the last reset. Gets truncated to the granularity of the underlying meter.|
|to|query|string(date-time)|false|End of time range to query entitlement: date-time in RFC 3339 format. Defaults to now.<br>If not now then gets truncated to the granularity of the underlying meter.|
|windowSize|query|[WindowSize](#schemawindowsize)|true|Windowsize|
|windowTimeZone|query|string|false|The timezone used when calculating the windows.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|windowSize|MINUTE|
|windowSize|HOUR|
|windowSize|DAY|
|windowSize|MONTH|

## Reset subject entitlement

<a id="opIdresetEntitlementUsage"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v1/subjects/string/entitlements/string/reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/problem+json' \
  -d '{
    "effectiveAt": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
    "retainAnchor": true,
    "preserveOverage": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/subjects/{subjectIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementId}/reset`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Reset marks the start of a new usage period for the entitlement and initiates grant rollover. At the start of a period usage is zerod out and grants are rolled over based on their rollover settings. It would typically be synced with the subjects billing period to enforce usage based on their subscription.

Usage is automatically reset for metered entitlements based on their usage period, but this endpoint allows to manually reset it at any time. When doing so the period anchor of the entitlement can be changed if needed.

⚠️ __Deprecated__: Use [`POST /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/reset`](#tag/entitlements/post/api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/reset) instead.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "effectiveAt": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
  "retainAnchor": true,
  "preserveOverage": true
}
```

<h3 id="reset-subject-entitlement-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|subjectIdOrKey|path|string|true|none|
|entitlementId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[ResetEntitlementUsageInput](#schemaresetentitlementusageinput)|true|none|
|» effectiveAt|body|string(date-time)|false|The time at which the reset takes effect, defaults to now. The reset cannot be in the future. The provided value is truncated to the minute due to how historical meter data is stored.|
|» retainAnchor|body|boolean|false|Determines whether the usage period anchor is retained or reset to the effectiveAt time.<br>- If true, the usage period anchor is retained.<br>- If false, the usage period anchor is reset to the effectiveAt time.|
|» preserveOverage|body|boolean|false|Determines whether the overage is preserved or forgiven, overriding the entitlement's default behavior.<br>- If true, the overage is preserved.<br>- If false, the overage is forgiven.|

## Create a customer entitlement

<a id="opIdcreateCustomerEntitlementV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v2/customers/01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH/entitlements \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "featureKey": "example-feature-key",
    "featureId": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
    "metadata": {
      "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
    },
    "type": "metered",
    "isSoftLimit": false,
    "usagePeriod": {
      "interval": "DAY",
      "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
    },
    "measureUsageFrom": {},
    "preserveOverageAtReset": false,
    "issueAfterReset": 0,
    "issueAfterResetPriority": 1,
    "issue": {
      "amount": 0,
      "priority": 1
    },
    "grants": [
      {
        "amount": 100,
        "priority": 1,
        "effectiveAt": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
        "minRolloverAmount": 100,
        "metadata": {
          "stripePaymentId": "pi_4OrAkhLvyihio9p51h9iiFnB"
        },
        "recurrence": {
          "interval": "DAY",
          "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
        },
        "maxRolloverAmount": 100,
        "expiration": {
          "duration": {},
          "count": 12
        },
        "annotations": {
          "internal_reference": "internal_reference"
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements`

OpenMeter has three types of entitlements: metered, boolean, and static. The type property determines the type of entitlement. The underlying feature has to be compatible with the entitlement type specified in the request (e.g., a metered entitlement needs a feature associated with a meter).

- Boolean entitlements define static feature access, e.g. "Can use SSO authentication".
- Static entitlements let you pass along a configuration while granting access, e.g. "Using this feature with X Y settings" (passed in the config).
- Metered entitlements have many use cases, from setting up usage-based access to implementing complex credit systems.  Example: The customer can use 10000 AI tokens during the usage period of the entitlement.

A given customer can only have one active (non-deleted) entitlement per featureKey. If you try to create a new entitlement for a featureKey that already has an active entitlement, the request will fail with a 409 error.

Once an entitlement is created you cannot modify it, only delete it.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "featureKey": "example-feature-key",
  "featureId": "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "metadata": {
    "externalId": "019142cc-a016-796a-8113-1a942fecd26d"
  },
  "type": "metered",
  "isSoftLimit": false,
  "usagePeriod": {
    "interval": "DAY",
    "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
  },
  "measureUsageFrom": {},
  "preserveOverageAtReset": false,
  "issueAfterReset": 0,
  "issueAfterResetPriority": 1,
  "issue": {
    "amount": 0,
    "priority": 1
  },
  "grants": [
    {
      "amount": 100,
      "priority": 1,
      "effectiveAt": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
      "minRolloverAmount": 100,
      "metadata": {
        "stripePaymentId": "pi_4OrAkhLvyihio9p51h9iiFnB"
      },
      "recurrence": {
        "interval": "DAY",
        "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
      },
      "maxRolloverAmount": 100,
      "expiration": {
        "duration": {},
        "count": 12
      },
      "annotations": {
        "internal_reference": "internal_reference"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

|---|---|---|---|---|

## Delete customer entitlement

<a id="opIddeleteCustomerEntitlementV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v2/customers/01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH/entitlements/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/problem+json'
```

`DELETE /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}`

Deleting an entitlement revokes access to the associated feature. As a single customer can only have one entitlement per featureKey, when "migrating" features you have to delete the old entitlements as well.
As access and status checks can be historical queries, deleting an entitlement populates the deletedAt timestamp. When queried for a time before that, the entitlement is still considered active, you cannot have retroactive changes to access, which is important for, among other things, auditing.

<h3 id="delete-customer-entitlement-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customerIdOrKey|path|[ULIDOrExternalKey](#schemaulidorexternalkey)|true|none|
|entitlementIdOrFeatureKey|path|string|true|none|

## Create customer entitlement grant

<a id="opIdcreateCustomerEntitlementGrantV2"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://openmeter.cloud/api/v2/customers/01G65Z755AFWAKHE12NY0CQ9FH/entitlements/string/grants \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "amount": 100,
    "priority": 1,
    "effectiveAt": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
    "minRolloverAmount": 100,
    "metadata": {
      "stripePaymentId": "pi_4OrAkhLvyihio9p51h9iiFnB"
    },
    "recurrence": {
      "interval": "DAY",
      "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
    },
    "maxRolloverAmount": 100,
    "expiration": {
      "duration": {},
      "count": 12
    },
    "annotations": {
      "internal_reference": "internal_reference"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v2/customers/{customerIdOrKey}/entitlements/{entitlementIdOrFeatureKey}/grants`

Grants define a behavior of granting usage for a metered entitlement. They can have complicated recurrence and rollover rules, thanks to which you can define a wide range of access patterns with a single grant, in most cases you don't have to periodically create new grants. You can only issue grants for active metered entitlements.

A grant defines a given amount of usage that can be consumed for the entitlement. The grant is in effect between its effective date and its expiration date. Specifying both is mandatory for new grants.

Grants have a priority setting that determines their order of use. Lower numbers have higher priority, with 0 being the highest priority.

Grants can have a recurrence setting intended to automate the manual reissuing of grants. For example, a daily recurrence is equal to reissuing that same grant every day (ignoring rollover settings).

Rollover settings define what happens to the remaining balance of a grant at a reset. Balance_After_Reset = MIN(MaxRolloverAmount, MAX(Balance_Before_Reset, MinRolloverAmount))

Grants cannot be changed once created, only deleted. This is to ensure that balance is deterministic regardless of when it is queried.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 100,
  "priority": 1,
  "effectiveAt": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z",
  "minRolloverAmount": 100,
  "metadata": {
    "stripePaymentId": "pi_4OrAkhLvyihio9p51h9iiFnB"
  },
  "recurrence": {
    "interval": "DAY",
    "anchor": "2023-01-01T01:01:01.001Z"
  },
  "maxRolloverAmount": 100,
  "expiration": {
    "duration": {},
    "count": 12
  },
  "annotations": {
    "internal_reference": "internal_reference"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-customer-entitlement-grant-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|customerIdOrKey|path|[ULIDOrExternalKey](#schemaulidorexternalkey)|true|none|
|entitlementIdOrFeatureKey|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[EntitlementGrantCreateInputV2](#schemaentitlementgrantcreateinputv2)|true|none|
|» amount|body|number(double)|true|The amount to grant. Should be a positive number.|
|» priority|body|integer(uint8)|false|The priority of the grant. Grants with higher priority are applied first.<br>Priority is a positive decimal numbers. With lower numbers indicating higher importance.<br>For example, a priority of 1 is more urgent than a priority of 2.<br>When there are several grants available for the same subject, the system selects the grant with the highest priority.<br>In cases where grants share the same priority level, the grant closest to its expiration will be used first.<br>In the case of two grants have identical priorities and expiration dates, the system will use the grant that was created first.|
|» effectiveAt|body|string(date-time)|true|Effective date for grants and anchor for recurring grants. Provided value will be ceiled to metering windowSize (minute).|
|» minRolloverAmount|body|number(double)|false|Grants are rolled over at reset, after which they can have a different balance compared to what they had before the reset.<br>Balance after the reset is calculated as: Balance_After_Reset = MIN(MaxRolloverAmount, MAX(Balance_Before_Reset, MinRolloverAmount))|
|» metadata|body|object|false|The grant metadata.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» recurrence|body|object|false|The subject of the grant.|
|» » interval|body|object|true|The unit of time for the interval.|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|string|false|none|
|» » » *anyOf*|body|[RecurringPeriodIntervalEnum](#schemarecurringperiodintervalenum)|false|The unit of time for the interval.<br>One of: `day`, `week`, `month`, or `year`.|
|» » anchor|body|string(date-time)|false|A date-time anchor to base the recurring period on.|
|» maxRolloverAmount|body|number(double)|false|Grants are rolled over at reset, after which they can have a different balance compared to what they had before the reset. The default value equals grant amount.<br>Balance after the reset is calculated as: Balance_After_Reset = MIN(MaxRolloverAmount, MAX(Balance_Before_Reset, MinRolloverAmount))|
|» expiration|body|object|false|The grant expiration definition. If no expiration is provided, the grant can be active indefinitely.|
|» » duration|body|object|true|The unit of time for the expiration period.|
|» » count|body|integer(uint32)|true|The number of time units in the expiration period.|
|» annotations|body|object|false|Grant annotations|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
